title: Titus 3: salvation by mercy, not works of righteousness
source_text: XXI. Et certe pars illa salutis, cujus per Dei gratiam in hac vita sumus participes, prae-cipue consistit in liberatione a servitute peccati, & adeptione verae justitiae & sanctitatis: Et tamen Apostolus salutem illam operibus abrogat, cap. tertio epistolae ad Titum. Quum autem, inquit, benignitas & erga homines amor apparuit Salvatoris nostri Dei, non ex operibus justitiae quae fecimus nos, sed secundum suam misericordiam salvos nos fecit, per lavacrum regenerationis, & renovationem Spiritus Sancti, quem effudit in nos abunde per Jesum Christum Servatorem nostrum. Ubi opera justitiae quae ipsi fecimus oppo-nit lavacro regenerationis, & renovationi per Spiritum Sanctum: ac salutem nostram (id est, redemptionem a peccato, sive a servitute & sordibus peccati, cum vera justitia & sanctitate conjunctam) tribui non vult operibus illis, ut causae efficienti, sive merito-riae; sed operationi Spiritus nos renovantis atque regenerantis, ut ita res sint oppositae, ex operibus esse & per Spiritus gratiam fieri.
pass_a_gloss: And certainly that part of salvation of which by God's grace we are partakers in this life consists chiefly in liberation from the slavery of sin and the obtaining of true righteousness and holiness. And yet the Apostle takes that salvation away from works in the third chapter of the epistle to Titus. But when, he says, the kindness and love toward men of God our Savior appeared, he saved us, not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy, by the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit, whom he poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior. Where he opposes the works of righteousness which we ourselves have done to the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit; and he will not have our salvation (that is, redemption from sin, or from the slavery and filth of sin, joined with true righteousness and holiness) ascribed to those works as efficient or meritorious cause, but to the operation of the Spirit renewing and regenerating us, so that the things are opposed: to be of works, and to be made by the Spirit's grace.
pass_b_english: The salvation we already share is chiefly freedom from sin's slavery and true holiness—yet Titus 3 denies it is from works of righteousness we did.
It is by mercy through washing of regeneration and Spirit renewal.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1055.
